subject: Streaming parse failures affecting checkout widgets - urgent
messages:
From: ops@quickretail.io

Cc: support@quickretail.io
Date: 2026-10-04T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: High error rate + latency on streaming checkout responses since SDK rollout

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing elevated 5xx errors and long tail latency on streaming responses for our checkout widget after we rolled the new QuickRetail frontend yesterday (SDK v1.5.0). Impact is visible across all regions but particularly bad in us-west where we run most traffic.

Symptoms:
- ~12% increase in request error rate (mostly 502/504) for streaming endpoints, starting ~2026-10-04 13:10 PDT.
- Long tail token latency: some streams stall for 8-20s before failing.
- Errors correlate with large payloads (~1.2–1.6k token prompts) and when concurrent streams > 4.

Attached: stream-trace-2026-10-04.txt (excerpted SDK traces and server-side correlation ids). Screenshot attached showing the failed checkout session.

Can you triage urgently? This is affecting a handful of merchants and we've got pressure from their ops teams. If this looks like something on our side we'll roll back but want to confirm root cause before doing that.

Thanks,
Adam Chen
Platform Ops — QuickRetail
ops@quickretail.io

Subject: URGENT: QuickRetail streaming parse failures — please investigate (customer-impacting)

Team,

Customer QuickRetail is reporting a spike of streaming parse failures and long tail stalls after their frontend rolled SDK v1.5.0. Logs attached by customer show lots of "stream parse: malformed header" and intermittent 502s. Impact looks severe in us-west.

Key data from customer:
- Approx start: 2026-10-04 13:10 PDT
- Request profile: large prompts (1k–1.6k tokens), concurrent streaming connections frequently >4
- Customer tried rolling back to v1.4.1 but reports the error rate dropped only slightly (not fully mitigated).

Please prioritize:
- Reproduce locally against SDK v1.5.0 with a traffic generator (match concurrency).
- Check the streaming parser for header-contiguity assumptions (multi-line header tokens split across frames).
- If you can root cause within 2 hours, produce a short mitigation we can give the customer (rollback, config toggle, or quick patch).

I will request an exec call if we need to commit credits / SLA exceptions. Customer is sensitive.

Thanks,
Soojin

--
Attachment: stream-trace-2026-10-04.txt (from customer, forwarded)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
To: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-04T19:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: QuickRetail streaming parse failures — please investigate (customer-impacting)

Soojin — I reproduced a similar failure pattern in our staging using the customer's trace and a synthetic generator with the SDK v1.5.0 client. Summary of findings:

1) Root cause hypothesis:
   - The client SDK's streaming parser assumes header lines are atomic within a single chunk. In high-concurrency, high-throughput conditions frames are split mid-header ("x-user-meta: ..."), which the parser doesn't stitch properly. This causes a malformed-header state and a subsequent parser exception that tears down the stream early.

2) Why rollback only partially helped:
   - Rolling to v1.4.1 reduces the occurrence but doesn't eliminate it because server-side runtime behavior (kernel selection + batching) can still create chunk boundaries that produce the split. 

3) Proposed short-term mitigations (to communicate to customer):
   - Set SDK option streaming:false for the checkout route (fall back to non-streaming endpoint) — fastest mitigation.
   - If non-streaming unacceptable, throttle concurrent_streams to 2 for the checkout route and enable prefix-caching on the server to reduce long prompts.
   - Patch: we have a small parser hardening fix (see attached). It detects partial header tokens across chunks and re-assembles them before parsing. Patch should be safe to roll as a micro-release (v1.5.1).

4) Risk and rollout plan:
   - Patch is low-risk (parser-level), create a canary with 5% of checkout traffic for 1 hour. If green, promote to 25% then 100% over 2–3 hours.

I'm attaching a minimal PR/patch: sdk-fix-stream-parser-PR.patch. I can open the PR and a canary deployment pipeline; will need infra sign-off for the canary window.

Rishi
Sr. Software Engineer — Serving Runtime
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

--
Attachment: sdk-fix-stream-parser-PR.patch (text, 12KB)

From: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
To: ops@quickretail.io
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-04T20:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + latency on streaming checkout responses since SDK rollout

Hi Adam — update from engineering: we've reproduced the issue and identified a parser hardening fix. Short-term options for you:

1) Easiest (1–2 minutes): Toggle streaming:false on the checkout route. This will route requests to the non-streaming path while we patch.
2) If you must keep streaming: set max_concurrent_streams to 2 for the checkout endpoint and we will enable prefix caching on our side to reduce prompt sizes.
3) We will prepare v1.5.1 (micro-release) with the parser fix and recommend a canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%). Rishi has attached a patch and can open the PR immediately.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow (Oct 5) at 09:00 PDT with our engineering and account leads to coordinate the rollout. We can also offer a billing credit for the impacted window if you decide to stay on streaming while we patch.

Please confirm which mitigation you want us to help implement (rollback, toggle streaming, throttle concurrent streams), and whether you'd like the 09:00 PDT call.

Thanks for the quick coordination.

Best,
Soojin Lee
